Kamau Therapeutics Receives FDA Regenerative Medicine Advanced Therapy (RMAT) Designation for Nula-cel, a Gene-Corrected Stem Cell Therapy for Sickle Cell Disease

Designation based on preliminary clinical evidence from the Phase 1/2 RESTORE trial; nula-cel also holds Fast Track and Orphan Drug designations

SOUTH SAN FRANCISCO, Calif., Nov. 12, 2026 — Kamau Therapeutics, a clinical-stage company creating medicines that endure by precisely engineering patients’ own blood stem cells, today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted Regenerative Medicine Advanced Therapy (RMAT) designation to nula-cel, an investigational stem cell medicine for sickle cell disease. The designation is based on preliminary clinical evidence from the ongoing Phase 1/2 RESTORE trial.

In RESTORE, all three patients treated with the optimized manufacturing process achieved transfusion independence with no vaso-occlusive events. The two patients with more than six months of follow-up have sickle hemoglobin below 20%, under the 30% threshold targeted for stroke prevention, with a predominantly adult hemoglobin profile.

RMAT designation is granted when preliminary clinical evidence indicates that a regenerative medicine therapy has the potential to address unmet medical needs in a serious condition. Designated therapies receive early, frequent FDA engagement and may be eligible for priority review and accelerated approval.

“Pain crises matter, but between them, sickled cells continue damaging the body. That is why guidelines call for exchange transfusions to keep sickle hemoglobin below 30% to prevent stroke,” said Vali Barsan, MD, Chief Executive Officer of Kamau Therapeutics. “We designed nula-cel to correct the root cause of sickle cell disease in a single treatment, and our team’s tireless work across research, manufacturing, quality, and clinical development has brought it into the clinic. This designation recognizes early clinical evidence of that correction as we advance nula-cel towards more patients.”

“RMAT designation grants us enhanced, more frequent interactions with the FDA as we plan the next stage of clinical development,” added Jacob Garcia, MD, Chief Medical Officer of Kamau Therapeutics. “We plan to request a comprehensive multidisciplinary RMAT meeting the agency recommended to align on the path to a registrational dataset, including the potential for priority review and endpoints for accelerated approval. We look forward to sharing additional interim efficacy data from RESTORE later this year.”

#### About Nula-cel

Nula-cel is an investigational stem cell medicine for sickle cell disease. Rather than inducing fetal hemoglobin to compensate for the disease, nula-cel is designed to correct the sickle mutation itself, converting it to the normal adult β-globin sequence. Using ex vivo homology-directed repair (HDR), Kamau precisely engineers a patient’s own long-lived stem cells outside the body, rigorously verifying each cell product’s quality, identity, potency, and safety before it is returned to the patient, a level of control not possible when editing occurs inside the body. As these cells self-renew, a one-time treatment is designed to deliver durable, potentially lifelong benefit. In the ongoing Phase 1/2 RESTORE trial (NCT04819841), nula-cel has shown transfusion independence and no vaso-occlusive events in all three patients treated with the optimized manufacturing process, and sickle hemoglobin below 20% with a predominantly adult hemoglobin profile in the two patients with more than six months of follow-up. Nula-cel has received RMAT, Fast Track, and Orphan Drug designations from the FDA.

#### About Sickle Cell Disease

Sickle cell disease (SCD) is an inherited blood disorder affecting approximately 100,000 people in the United States and millions globally. A single mutation in the β-globin gene produces sickle hemoglobin (HgbS), which polymerizes, stiffening red cells and driving chronic hemolysis. Pain crises are the visible burden; chronic organ damage, including stroke and injury to the kidneys, retinas, and bones, accumulates silently between them, shortening U.S. life expectancy by decades. While approved pharmacologic and gene therapies reduce pain crises, none restores native adult hemoglobin (HgbA) or consistently achieves the sustained HgbS levels below 30% that ASH guidelines associate with stroke prevention in chronic exchange transfusion protocols.

#### About Kamau Therapeutics

Kamau Therapeutics is a clinical-stage company developing a new generation of stem cell medicines designed to create lasting benefit through a single intervention. Kamau’s platform precisely engineers long-lived stem cells outside the body, providing control to select, modify, characterize, and verify cells before they return to the patient. As these cells self-renew and continually produce new cells, a change made once has the potential to endure. Kamau’s approach is built on homology-directed repair (HDR), the high-fidelity pathway cells naturally use to repair their own DNA, which Kamau has engineered to be efficient and reproducible in hematopoietic stem cells. Kamau’s lead program, nula-cel, is an investigational therapy for sickle cell disease designed to directly correct the sickle-causing mutation at its native location in the β-globin gene, restoring production of adult hemoglobin under the body’s own regulation rather than relying on fetal hemoglobin. Kamau’s integrated, cross-functional team, many of whom have advanced nula-cel from bench to bedside, is united by a single purpose: delivering stem cell medicines to patients. ## Novo submits etavopivat, an investigational once-daily therapy for adolescents and adults living with sickle cell disease, to the FDA and EMA for approval

  * The FDA New Drug Application (NDA) and EMA Marketing Authorization Application (MAA) submissions for etavopivat are based on data from the Phase 3 HIBISCUS trial showing efficacy and safety results in adolescents and adults living with sickle cell disease^{1}
  * Sickle cell disease is a progressive, life-threatening, debilitating blood disease with limited disease-modifying therapeutic options that affects an estimated 100,000 Americans, 110,000 Europeans – and around 8 million people worldwide^{2-4}
  * Etavopivat is designed to help reduce the sickling of red blood cells and is being evaluated for potential improvement of haemoglobin response (>1 g/dL) rate at week 24 and the reduction of annualized ‘vaso-occlusive crises’ (VOCs) rates at week 52^{1}

Plainsboro, New Jersey, US and Bagsværd, Denmark, 12 November 2026 – Novo Nordisk today announced the submissions of a New Drug Application (NDA) to the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and a Marketing Authorization Application (MAA) to the European Medicines Agency (EMA) for etavopivat, an investigational, once-daily, orally available, selective activator of pyruvate kinase red blood cell isozyme (PKR), for the treatment of adolescents and adults (aged 12 years and older) living with sickle cell disease (SCD). If approved, etavopivat could offer a new approach to treating SCD as a disease-modifying therapy.

The FDA has previously granted etavopivat Fast Track, Rare Pediatric Disease and Orphan Drug designations and is expected to take action on the NDA in 2027. Etavopivat was also granted Orphan Drug designation by the European Commission, which is expected to take action on the MAA in 2027. An MAA is the formal application for seeking approval to market a medicine in the European Union (EU).

"For people living with sickle cell disease, severe vaso-occlusive crises and other symptoms can have a profound impact on everyday life, and treatment options remain limited," said Martin Holst Lange, executive vice president, chief scientific officer and head of Research & Development at Novo. “If approved, we are hopeful that etavopivat can provide a new disease-modifying treatment option for people living with sickle cell disease, and we will continue to work alongside the community to help advance health equity and overcome the longstanding disparities that impact those affected by this disease."

The NDA and MAA submissions are grounded in the results from the HIBISCUS study program, which was designed to establish the efficacy and safety profile of etavopivat, and evaluated the annualised rate of vaso-occlusive crises (VOCs) at week 52 and haemoglobin response (> 1 g/dL) rate at week 24 compared to placebo, in adults and adolescents living with SCD. Participants were also allowed to receive standard-of-care treatment throughout the trial.^{1 }In topline results announced in April 2026, etavopivat showed a 27% reduction in VOCs and a ~4-month delay to the first VOC compared to placebo. More detailed results from the HIBISCUS phase 3 trial will be presented at a future scientific conference and published in a peer-reviewed journal.

What is sickle cell disease?
Sickle cell disease (SCD) is driven by polymerisation of mutated sickle haemoglobin (HbS) in red blood cells. The two main hallmarks of SCD are hemolytic anaemia and vaso-occlusive crises (VOCs). Around 8 million people worldwide live with SCD, with the majority in low- and middle-income countries.The increase in ATP production helps preserve RBC membrane integrity and deformability, improving RBC survival. These disease-modifying effects have the potential to reduce VOC events and improve Hb levels.

The US Food and Drug Administration has granted etavopivat Fast Track, Rare Pediatric Disease and Orphan Drug designations. Additionally, etavopivat was granted Orphan Drug designation by the European Commission based on a positive opinion from the Committee for Orphan Medicinal Products of the European Medicines Agency for the treatment of patients with SCD.

Etavopivat was acquired by Novo as part of the 2022 acquisition of Forma Therapeutics.

What is the HIBISCUS programme?
The HIBISCUS clinical development programme investigates etavopivat as a disease-modifying treatment for people with SCD. The pivotal programme includes:

HIBISCUS (NCT04624659) - a 52-week efficacy and safety design phase 2/3 trial, comparing once-daily etavopivat versus placebo, enrolling approximately 440 people aged 12 years and over with SCD who had 2 to 15 VOCs within 12 months prior to enrollment. Participants were allowed to receive standard-of-care treatment throughout the trial. Following the completion of the 12-week phase 2 interim readout, the phase 3 dose was selected, and participants were randomised to the phase 3 main phase of the trial, which continued for 52 weeks.^{1}

HIBISCUS 2 (NCT06612268) - a 52-week efficacy and safety phase 3b trial, comparing once-daily etavopivat versus placebo, with expected enrollment of 510 people aged 12 years and older with SCD.^{1}

FLORAL (NCT06609226) – an open-label extension following participation in etavopivat trials. The study allows the collection of long-term safety data.^{1}
